review.notes: IMG_5390 is visibly headed Sound of Luing. Its Tides and Dangers material continues from the left into the top of the right column, followed by clipped initial Sound Directions. The discrete paragraph beginning 'The photograph...' through the next blue Anchorage heading is Corryvreckan-focused and excluded; separately headed Anchorage is outside gate evidence. The Sound section says tide changes are on average, then gives separate north-going spring/neap beginnings of +270/+315 min and south-going beginnings of -105/-60 min against Oban; the prior notation key supplies the HW meaning. The passage-level 15-minute spring and 60-minute neap slack durations have no turn assignment or placement. Both flood and ebb vary spatially from a stated 3 kn springs at Ardluing to maxima of 7 kn springs and 5 kn neaps among islands around Fladda, so the values are not copied into turn records or assigned to the broad OS named-sea point. The source also describes a local ebb continuing about one hour after mid-channel flood begins, a clipped drying obstruction associated with Belnahua, and course-keeping cautions around overfalls and current. No true bearing, supported flow model or reference-range interpolation is stated. Outer/right and lower Sound text is clipped, so Dangers and Directions remain incomplete. The positive v2 operational checklist therefore fails closed; the legacy Sound of Luing Location and v1 gate remain unchanged.

cautions.summary: The source says the last of the ebb along the Lunga shore can continue for approximately 60 minutes after the flood begins in mid-channel; no route-specific asynchronous-turn model is supplied.

The Sound of Luing Dangers block continues into the top of IMG_5390's right column, followed by clipped initial Sound Directions. The discrete Corryvreckan-focused paragraph beginning 'The photograph...' is excluded through the next blue Anchorage heading, and separately headed Anchorage is outside gate evidence, so target hazards and passage directions are not exhaustively captured.

The visible initial Sound Directions gives broad course-keeping cautions around overfalls and current, including risk of being set off course under sail in light winds, but the right edge clips wording and locality so no route or manoeuvring rule is encoded.

hazards.summary: The source describes a flood race north of Rubha Fiola continuing west of Ormsa and Belnahua, plus an eddy off Rubha na Lic whose side changes between flood and ebb; the named-sea point supplies no exact race or eddy locus or dynamic model.

The visible Dangers material identifies the drying Rubh Ard Luing at the southeast entrance with rocks extending around it and a charted buoy/berth instruction; the block continues into the right column, but clipped outer/lower text prevents exhaustive hazard capture and the broad name point is not a safe-water or clearance position.

The top-right continuation of Sound Dangers describes an incompletely captured drying obstruction associated with Belnahua, extending about 3 cables and drying 0.3 metre; its feature and direction are clipped, so no actionable hazard geometry is encoded.

review.notes: IMG_5387 is headed Sound of Jura - east side and shows only the start of a new 'Approach to ...' heading because the photographed edge clips its object. IMG_5388 starts at Tides and is attributable to Dorus Mòr from repeated internal naming and the new Corryvreckan boundary on IMG_5389, but the complete primary heading and page identity are unavailable. The body applies 8 kn springs and 6 kn neaps jointly to flood and ebb, says the fastest rate is within the first two hours, names flood east-to-west and ebb west-to-east through Dorus, and gives compound north/west and south/east spring/neap beginnings of +270/+315 and -105/-60 min against Oban. Prolonged strong west winds can advance the times considerably. Passage-level slack of 15 minutes springs and 60 minutes neaps has no turn scope or placement. Printed 191 and 151 degree clearing-line bearings are not current directions. No exact rate locus, true stream bearing, supported flow model or reference-range interpolation is stated. Outer and bottom hazard/direction text is clipped. The positive v2 operational checklist therefore fails closed; the legacy Dorus Mòr Location and v1 gate remain unchanged.

cautions.summary: The source says prolonged strong west winds can advance the stated turn beginnings considerably and supplies no numerical correction or precision bound.
The printed 191 and 151 degree bearings are clearing-mark alignments, not current-towards bearings, and must not be used to complete either turn direction.

The permitted photographs do not show the complete primary Dorus Mòr heading or page identity, and clip outer/bottom Dangers and Directions text; the target section is internally attributable but not exhaustively captured.

hazards.summary: The source says turbulence and overfalls increase after prolonged strong west winds and especially when wind opposes tide; no bounded timing, sea-state or locality model is supplied.

For the flood, the source describes branching streams, a race east of Reisa Mhic Phaidean, eddies at Craignish Point and Garbh Reisa, and turbulence or overfalls across the Dorus Mòr, Reisa an t-Sruith and Coiresa area; the channel representative localizes none of these.

For the ebb, the source identifies the strongest stream on the south side near Garbh Reisa, converging flows and overfalls southeast of Rubha na Una, and heavy northwest-entrance overfalls plus confused seas in strong southerly wind; no exact operational hazard model is supplied.

The visible Dangers text identifies a submerged rock about half a mile northwest of Craignish Point toward Coiresa with 0.6 metre over it, while further rock and clearing-mark details are clipped; the channel point is not a clearance or safe-water position.

uncertainty.summary: The joined Location's own OS Open Names provenance defines a naming point for a roughly 1.26 by 1.05 kilometre Dorus Mòr Channel feature, not a surveyed gate, exact fairway, safe-water point, route, rate station or exact stream, turn, slack, rate, eddy, race or overfall locus.

The source gives spring/neap north- or west-going beginnings of +270/+315 min and south- or east-going beginnings of -105/-60 min relative to HW Oban, but says prolonged strong west winds can advance them considerably without a correction or precision bound.
The source reports passage-level slack durations of 15 minutes at springs and 60 minutes at neaps, but does not assign either to an individual turn or define centred, before or after placement.

The source says both flood and ebb reach 8 kn at springs and 6 kn at neaps, with the fastest rate within the first two hours. These passage-wide shared values have no exact rate locus and are not copied into individual turn records or assigned to the broad OS channel point as exact gate-local observations.
The supplied photographs show no complete Dorus Mòr heading, publication title, publisher, edition or target page number, so the operational structured-source requirement is incomplete.
